name: Boma Nkuu
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

tone_statements.citation: Nsuka Nkutsi, François. 1990. Note sur les parlers teke du Zaïre. Pholia 5: 147–173. Lyon: CRLS, Université Lumière-Lyon 2.
tone_statements.quote: En dépouillant les matériaux recueillis jusqu'ici sur les quatre dialectes, plusieurs points ont retenu notre attention : la tonalité, l'accent et la morphologie du système nominal présentent des écarts notables par rapport aux dialectes teke du Congo et du Gabon. Nous avons cependant limité notre article à l'examen des sons et des phonèmes à cause essentiellement de l'importance inégale des données à propos des quatre dialectes (par exemple, liste de 630 mots pour le boma et de seulement 200 mots sur chacun des trois autres dialectes).
tone_statements.translation: In working through the material collected so far on the four dialects, several points caught our attention: tonality, accent and the morphology of the nominal system show notable divergences from the Teke dialects of Congo and Gabon. We have nevertheless limited our article to the examination of sounds and phonemes, essentially because of the unequal amount of data on the four dialects (for example, a list of 630 words for boma and only 200 words for each of the three other dialects).

sources.citation: Nsuka Nkutsi, François. 1990. Note sur les parlers teke du Zaïre. Pholia 5: 147–173. Lyon: CRLS, Université Lumière-Lyon 2.
sources.note: The only primary description of Nkuu: a 200-word list (informant Tswemi Ntumi Emmanuel, Kinshasa 1988–89) plus C/V inventories and syllable structure for four Zaire Teke dialects (boma = South Boma B80y, nkuu = Boma Nkuu B80x, bibaana, ngi). Every form carries H/L tone marks (acute/grave). On accent it says only (p. 148, Avant-propos) that tone, accent and nominal morphology show notable divergences from the Teke dialects of Congo and Gabon, and that the article is deliberately limited to sounds and phonemes; it never states where stress/accent falls. p. 164: nkuu has lost the final vowel of…

tone.quote: En dépouillant les matériaux recueillis jusqu'ici sur les quatre dialectes, plusieurs points ont retenu notre attention : la tonalité, l'accent et la morphologie du système nominal présentent des écarts notables par rapport aux dialectes teke du Congo et du Gabon. Nous avons cependant limité notre article à l'examen des sons et des phonèmes à cause essentiellement de l'importance inégale des données à propos des quatre dialectes (par exemple, liste de 630 mots pour le boma et de seulement 200 mots sur chacun des trois autres dialectes).
tone.translation: In working through the material collected so far on the four dialects, several points caught our attention: tonality, accent and the morphology of the nominal system show notable divergences from the Teke dialects of Congo and Gabon. We have nevertheless limited our article to the examination of sounds and phonemes, essentially because of the unequal amount of data on the four dialects (for example, a list of 630 words for boma and only 200 words for each of the three other dialects).
tone.says: First-hand but minimal: the author states that tonality, accent and nominal morphology of the four Zaire Teke dialects (boma, nkuu, bibaana, ngi) show notable differences from the Teke dialects of Congo and Gabon, and that the article is deliberately limited to sounds and phonemes, deferring tone; every cited nkuu form is transcribed with H (acute) and L (grave) tone marks, with HL/LH sequences on long vowels. No tone inventory, rules or accent placement are given.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page boma1250 (Boma Nkuu) and reference records 586272, 700922
sources.note: Lists only the two Pacchiarotti et al. overview/comparative papers (2019, 2024); AES 'threatened'; comment quotes Pacchiarotti et al. 2019: 166 that Nkuu is 'a language in the linguistically poorly studied region engulfed by the Kwa, Congo and Kwango rivers of DRC'. No grammar, sketch, phonology or dictionary is listed.

sources.citation: Pacchiarotti, Sara, Guy Kouarata & Koen Bostoen. 2024. Sound change versus lexical change for subgrouping: Word-final lenition of Proto-Bantu *ŋg in West-Coastal Bantu. Language Dynamics and Change 14(2): 1–73 (author accepted manuscript).
sources.note: Comparative study of *ŋg lenition; Appendix item 32 'Nkuu (Camp-Bankuu) B80x DRC -3.42 17.26 Own fieldwork 2022' shows new BantUGent field data exist for Nkuu; tone marks uniformized across sources; no mention of stress or accent.

sources.citation: Pacchiarotti, Sara & Koen Bostoen. 2021. Final vowel loss in Lower Kasai Bantu (DRC) as a contact-induced change. Journal of Language Contact 14: 437–475.
sources.note: p. 447: Boma Nkuu B80x (Nsuka Nkutsi 1990) sporadically manifests final vowel loss 'as far as the very scanty available sources (mostly wordlists) allow us to observe'; excluded from the case study for paucity of data. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Pacchiarotti, Sara, Natalia Chousou-Polydouri & Koen Bostoen. 2019. Untangling the West-Coastal Bantu mess: identification, geography and phylogeny of the Bantu B50-80 languages. Africana Linguistica 25 (pp. 87–162 per Glottolog bib 586272).
sources.note: Section on 'Boma' glossonyms: 'To our knowledge, the only existing documentation on the language spoken by the Boma Nkuu is a wordlist found in Nsuka Nkutsi (1990)'; assigns the new code B80x, treats Boma Nkuu (Monkana) and South Boma Nkuu (Boku, B80y) as two distinct languages, and notes there was no glottocode or ISO code at the time. Classification/lexicostatistics only; nothing on stress or tone.

tone.quote: Le parler kenkuu tient son nom de l’activité exercée par ses locuteurs : nkúú/bànkúú ‘chasseur’. C’est une variété teke parlée en RDC, sur la rive gauche de la rivière Kwilu, dans le territoire de Kwamouth (province Mai‑Ndombe, villages Bishala, Lilala, Menkwo, Bibonga et Camp Banku). La comparaison de nos données lexicales pour cette variété avec celles disponibles dans Nsuka Nkutsi (1990) pour la variété qu’il appelle « nkuu », également connu sous le nom de « boma nkuu » (voir Pacchiarotti et al. 2019 : 166), montre qu’il s’agit de la même variété, comme le montre le tableau 4. [...] le nkuu a subi la perte systématique de voyelles finales dans tous les environnements phonotactiquement appropriés.
tone.locator: Sect. 5.1.2 '(Boma/buma) nkuu (B80x)', pp. 10-11; Tableau 4 on p. 11
tone.translation: The kenkuu variety takes its name from the activity of its speakers: nkúú/bànkúú 'hunter'. It is a Teke variety spoken in the DRC, on the left bank of the Kwilu river, in Kwamouth territory (Mai-Ndombe province, villages Bishala, Lilala, Menkwo, Bibonga and Camp Banku). Comparison of our lexical data for this variety with those available in Nsuka Nkutsi (1990) for the variety he calls 'nkuu', also known as 'boma nkuu' (see Pacchiarotti et al. 2019: 166), shows that it is the same variety, as Table 4 shows. [...] Nkuu has undergone the systematic loss of final vowels in all phonotactically appropriate environments.

sources.note: Closest full sketch of a neighbouring 'Boma' variety, but it describes North Boma B82 [boma1251], which Pacchiarotti et al. 2019 and Maselli 2024 treat as a distinct language from Boma Nkuu; useful only as a related-language proxy for the tone/accent type of the area, not as a statement about Nkuu.

sources.citation: Pacchiarotti, Sara, Koen Bostoen, Lorenzo Maselli et al. (BantUGent). 2022 fieldwork on Nkuu (Camp-Bankuu, B80x): wordlist and any forthcoming phonological sketch
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The 2024 LDC paper (Appendix no. 32) shows that the Ghent team collected their own Nkuu data in 2022; a sketch or phonology of Nkuu from this corpus would be the first modern description and the first place a tone/accent statement could appear. Nothing published yet as far as UGent biblio and Glottolog show.

sources.citation: Nsuka Nkutsi, François. Announced follow-up study of 'la tonalité, l'accent et la morphologie du système nominal' of the Zaire Teke dialects (boma, nkuu, bibaana, ngi), promised in Pholia 5 (1990: 148)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The 1990 note explicitly says accent in these dialects differs from other Teke and defers it to later work; no such publication was found in Pholia 6–9 tables of contents, Persée (Africana Linguistica), Crossref or OpenAlex. If it exists (e.g. an unpublished CRLS Lyon manuscript), it is the only candidate for a first-hand accent statement on Nkuu.
